osm_steps.step: All OSM features with a loose well-like name (input extract)

Name has a well word (well, wells, ffynnon, tobar, tober, tubber, fuaran, chibbyr, venton, clootie) as a word, which drops Wellington, Bridewell, Powell, Maxwell, Cromwell, Boswell, spa and spring names
Not a road, building, business, organisation or settlement by name; topographic words (hill, green, head ...) drop a name only when it does not end in the well word (word lists in code)
Tags not those of a different kind of feature (natural only spring, water or wetland; man_made only water_well; amenity only place_of_worship, drinking_water, fountain or watering_place)

Evidence it is a well: tagged as a spring or well, or as religious, or historic and named as a well, or (if untagged in the extract) named as a saint's, holy or folk well in two or more words; untagged one-word names (Holywell, Ladywell) and untagged Tober and Tobar names are dropped because most are places or townlands
After removing OSM duplicates (same name within 150 m)
Inside the study area (land of Britain, Ireland and the Isle of Man, within about 3 km of the coast)
After removing OSM features within 150 m of an NMS holy well

examples: Cranfield Holy Well and rag trees

eyes.label: Eyes (a cure, or a well of the eyes)

statue.label: A statue, shrine, grotto or cross at the well
